a2-unit-38.38.1 Visit Hannibal, Missouri:
Paulo: Visit Hannibal, Missouri. A travel agent describes its top attractions.
Paulo: Hannibal, on the Mississippi River about a hundred miles north of St. Louis, is where Mark Twain grew up. He was born in eighteen thirty-five in Florida, Missouri, and his family moved to Hannibal when he was four. You'll have a great day exploring the town.
Paulo: The first place you'll want to visit is the Mark Twain Boyhood Home and Museum. The Clemens family lived in the white house from about eighteen forty-four until eighteen fifty-three. Mark Twain's real name was Samuel Clemens. The museum has several historic buildings, including the Huckleberry Finn House.
Paulo: Outside the house, there's a white fence, just like the fence that Tom paints in The Adventures of Tom Sawyer. Everyone takes a photo there!
Paulo: If you have children, the best place to spend an afternoon is Mark Twain Cave, the oldest show cave in Missouri. Twain played there as a boy, and the cave is in Tom Sawyer too. Tours last about an hour.
Paulo: And if your feet hurt after walking around town, try a river cruise. The Mark Twain Riverboat has one-hour sightseeing cruises, and the guide tells stories about the river. There's also a dinner cruise in the evening.
Paulo: Another way to end your day is a visit to Rockcliffe Mansion, a big house on a hill above the town. It was finished in nineteen hundred, and some people say it's haunted! Twain visited Hannibal for the last time in nineteen oh two, and there was a reception for him at the mansion.
Paulo: Hannibal has so much to offer visitors. You'll never forget the day you visited this magical place.
